From 193e87143c290ec16838f5368adc0e0bc94eb931 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Oct 2016 11:06:47 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: spi-nor: Off by one in cqspi_setup_flash()

There are CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT elements in the ->f_pdata array so the >
should be >=.

Fixes: 140623410536 ('mtd: spi-nor: Add driver for Cadence Quad SPI Flash Controller')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Marek Vasut <marex@denx.de>
Signed-off-by: Cyrille Pitchen <cyrille.pitchen@atmel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
index d403ba7b8f43..944863be0320 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c
@@ -1082,7 +1082,7 @@ static int cqspi_setup_flash(struct cqspi_st *cqspi, struct device_node *np)
 			goto err;
 		}
 
-		if (cs > CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
+		if (cs >= CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
 			dev_err(dev, "Chip select %d out of range.\n", cs);
 			goto err;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/mtd/spi-nor/cadence-quadspi.c`**
   - The conditional check in the `cqspi_setup_flash` function was modified from:
     ```c
     if (cs > CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     if (cs >= CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
     ```
   - This change ensures that the chip select index `cs` is checked to be greater than or equal to `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT`, correcting an off-by-one error.

### Relationships

- The modification in `cadence-quadspi.c` addresses a bug identified in the previous implementation of the chip select validation logic. The change is directly related to the fix for the bug introduced in commit `140623410536`, which added the driver for the Cadence Quad SPI Flash Controller. The patch improves the robustness of the driver by ensuring that the chip select index does not exceed the maximum allowed value, thereby preventing potential out-of-bounds access.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (cs > CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
```
Reason:
This condition incorrectly checks if the chip select index `cs` is greater than the maximum allowed value `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT`. This allows for an out-of-bounds access to the `->f_pdata` array when `cs` equals `CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT`, which is an invalid index, leading to potential undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (cs >= CQSPI_MAX_CHIPSELECT) {
```
Reason:
This corrected condition ensures that the chip select index `cs` is checked to be less than the maximum allowed value, preventing any out-of-bounds access to the `->f_pdata` array and thus eliminating the risk of undefined behavior.
